text:
ben: Heads-up — ap-southeast1c showing a slow but steady rise in GPU Pending (small pods). Looks like allocator is rejecting single-gpu tiny pods because of a combination of node taints + hard affinity to `rack=fast-1`.
kai: Ugh. Is this the same shelf that had conntrack blips yesterday? Could be nodes marked unschedulable intermittently and leaving tiny slots fragmented.
diane: Can you paste `kubectl get pod -o wide` for a couple of stuck pods? wondering if they request fractional gang or use podAffinity (which our scheduler treats as strict)
ben: quick excerpt:
```
$ kubectl describe pod job-x-7b9
Node: gpu-apse1c-12
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 7 node(s) had taint {gpu-thermal: true}, 5 node(s) didn't match pod affinity/anti-affinity rules.
```
maria: That taint `gpu-thermal` is low-severity — autoscaler set it to prefer cooling nodes but it's blocking scheduling. ops-bot should be auto-untainting after 5m though.
ops-bot: [system] Detected 14 tainted nodes in ap-southeast1c with `gpu-thermal=true`. Auto-untaint job queued (ETA ~3m). Reaction: :gear:
kai: Even when taints clear, we might still have fragmentation: many tiny pods with nodeAffinity `rack=fast-1` and anti-affinity to `same-app` leaves holes. Scheduler prefers binpack by rack first which increases stranded single-GPU slots.
diane: Options:
- relax affinity (convert to preferredDuringScheduling) for small pods
- enable fractional gang packing (we've mocked a patch for multi-slot compaction)
- temporary bump on Dedicated pool capacity in ap-southeast1c
Which do we want to try first?
ben: Short-term: relax affinity + lower `preferredDuringScheduling` weight to 50 for ci/test pods. Mid: bump dedicated by 2 GPUs for next 6h. Long: revisit binpack policy for tiny-pod class.
maria: I'll open a canary PR to change affinity for job-x family and roll for 20% first. Also raising autoscaler headroom now.
diane: I'll queue the scheduler experiment (enable compaction heuristic) behind a canary toggle. Need a perf run post-rollout.
ben: Thanks — tagging @sam in case we need faster capacity provisioning.
maria: PR: https://git.company/repo/infra/PR-412 — changes prefAffinity weight and adds rationale. :thumbsup:
kai: Cool. Also leaving a note — if conntrack returns, fragmentation will spike again. Ops, can we add a probe to alert when headroom > 30% but pending pods > 5?
ops-bot: [system] Alert rule created: `ap-southeast1c_small_pod_fragmentation` threshold: pending_pods>=5 && headroom_pct>=30. Will notify #eng-oncall. Reaction: :white_check_mark:
ben: Good patch. We'll monitor for 1h after PR roll and revert if eviction churn increases.
